To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The average starting wage of the lowest paid occupations in establishments in the low-wage service sector is highly variable, with over half of the variation occurring across establishments within industries.

the variation in average and starting wages across establishments in a given industry is large, that the variation in the starting wages of the largest low wage occupations in a given industry and occupation is large, and that the variation in these wages can be explained in part by differences in the skills of the workforce and in part by differences across establishments in institutional factors.

1) the average establishment wages in low-wage industries vary substantially across establishments; 2) starting wages of the low-wage occupations vary substantially across establishments within industries; 3) a substantial portion of the intra-industry wage variation is explained by differences in worker skills and the institutional factors of unions, rent sharing and monitoring difficulty; and 4) the variation in starting wages of low-wage occupations across establishments is also substantially explained by worker skills and the same institutional factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the existence of and reasons for wage differentials within industries, and within the largest low-wage occupation in industries.
the following question: What accounts for the fact that the same industry in the same city can have different wages and starting wages for the same occupations?
intra-industry wage dispersion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intra-industry wage differential is due to both worker and establishment characteristics. (JEL: J31)
the intra-industry and intra-occupations wage differentials are the result of a combination of factors, but the most important are the skills of workers.

there is substantial intra-industry variation in both average establishment wages and starting wages of low-wage occupations that can be explained by differences in the skills of the workers, but also institutional factors such as union presence, monitoring difficulty, rent sharing, and difficulty in recruitment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the variation in average and starting wages of establishments is substantial, but the variation is not fully explained by differences in worker skills, and so institutional factors are also important.
the variation in intra-occupational and intra-industry wage variation is due to a combination of worker and institutional factors.
the skills of workers are a key determinant of the wage level of establishments, but that the institutional environment of establishments is also important.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intra-industry wage dispersion is large and is driven by both worker and establishment factors.
the wage differentials within industries and occupations are large and that they are due to factors that are not easily observable to the researcher.
there are important establishment-level factors that account for intra-industry and intra-occupatinal wage differentials.
